HEADLINE: One teen killed, others wounded, after explosion on Israeli school trip near Lebanon border

---BODY---
A border wall erected by Israel along its northern border with Lebanon is seen between Metulla in Israel to the right and Odaisseh in Lebanon to the left on June 19, 2026. Martin Grimes/Getty Images The Middle East See all topics Facebook Tweet Email Link Threads Link Copied! Follow One teenager was killed and others were wounded, according to Israeli emergency response services, after an explosion on an Israeli school trip near the Lebanon border.
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said an initial review by soldiers at the scene indicated that explosion was caused by an unexploded Hezbollah munition that had fallen in the area. It’s unclear when the projectile was fired. Pictures released by the IDF showed a military helicopter evacuating patients for medical treatment.
According to United Hatzalah, an Israeli emergency response service, three people sustained serious injuries in the explosion, while at least 10 others suffered light-to-moderate injuries.
In a statement, the Ma’alot-Tarshiha municipality in northern Israel said students and staff were on the local school’s annual trip when the explosion happened. The country’s Ministry of Education said it was an “extremely difficult incident, and our thoughts are with the victims and their families.”
Shortly after the explosion occurred on Monday afternoon, Israel Police said the initial suspicion was that the explosion was a result of an unexploded munition along the border near the villages of Yiftah and Manara. Bomb disposal experts were dispatched to examine the cause of the explosion, police said.
MDA said it was a “complex incident” as they sent numerous teams to the site. “We quickly dispatched substantial forces to the scene, including ambulances, mobile intensive care units (MICUs), and an MDA helicopter, which was also scrambled to the incident,” said regional director Itzik Shushan.
A US-brokered ceasefire in late-June was supposed to end months of conflict in southern Lebanon as it paved the way for the deployment of the Lebanese military and the gradual withdrawal of the IDF. Israel pulled back from two small areas along the so-called yellow line that demarcates the zone occupied by the Israeli military, but further progress on the agreement has largely stalled.
Israel has razed entire villages in southern Lebanon and has continued to carry out regular strikes there as it tries to remove Hezbollah from the territory.
